intent: A drift check that nobody runs is not a check. Install systemd units that run `setup_wireguard_ssh.sh verify` at every boot and daily, so a stale /etc/nftables.conf fails a unit instead of waiting to be noticed after every bridged container has silently lost the internet.
scope: Non-goal: changing the ruleset or the two invariants verify_nft already gates on
Non-goal: notifications; a failed unit in `systemctl --failed` is the gate
changes: New lib wg_verify_units.sh splits rendering from installing, the same way render/write_nftables_ruleset already do, so the generated unit CONTENT is assertable without a daemon-reload.

nftables-drift.service is Type=oneshot, After=nftables.service docker.service network-online.target. network-online.target is load-bearing: detect_lan_subnet shells out to `ip route get 1.1.1.1` and dies when there is no route, which at boot would be indistinguishable from real drift.

Deliberately NOT Requires=nftables.service: a dead nftables.service means the ruleset is not loaded at all, the most serious version of the fault, and the unit must run and fail rather than be skipped as unsatisfiable.

ProtectSystem=strict + ProtectHome=read-only: verify only reads, and the saved LAN_SUBNET lives in the repo under $HOME, where a root-owned rewrite would lock the non-root subcommands out of their own config. The unit makes that write impossible instead of merely unlikely.
ExecStart points at the repo checkout, not a copy under /usr/local/bin: the check is 'does /etc match what THIS repo generates', and a stale copy of a drift detector agrees with the drift.

The units are installed by `setup`, by `allow-web` and `allow-dns` (the commands that regenerate /etc/nftables.conf, so exactly when the check must exist), and by a new `install-verify` subcommand for retrofitting an existing machine.

Bumped the gatelock pin gattag v0.7.2 -> v0.7.3 in meta/requirements.txt to clear a pre-existing red dependency-freshness baseline on main, unrelated to this change but blocking the commit via the ci-baseline-green hook.

verification.evidence: 12 passed, 0 failed. Asserts ExecStart, Type=oneshot, all three After= orderings, the absence of Requires=, both Protect* settings, WantedBy=multi-user.target, and the timer's Unit=/Persistent=/WantedBy=.
The whole features/lib suite passes under the jail with the new file added; exit 0, no FAIL lines. Same invocation meta/scripts/ci_mirror_shell.sh uses pre-push.

verification.command: vm run nftdrift 'sudo setup_wireguard_ssh.sh install-verify' then a reboot with /etc/nftables.conf drifted
verification.evidence: Boot-time run FAILED as required: `systemctl is-failed` -> failed; `systemctl --failed` lists it; the journal carries the unified diff of the removed `iifname "docker0" accept` line AND '[ERROR] live forward chain does NOT accept docker0 -- bridged containers have no network.' Both invariants fired.

verification.command: vm run nftdrift 'sudo setup_wireguard_ssh.sh allow-web' then a second reboot
verification.evidence: No false positive: unit active, journal shows '[ OK ] /etc/nftables.conf matches what this script generates.' and '[ OK ] live forward chain lets Docker through.'; systemctl --failed count for it is 0; timer armed for 00:00.

verification.command: sudo linux_configuration/features/setup_wireguard_ssh.sh install-verify && sudo systemctl start nftables-drift.service (host)
verification.evidence: Installed and enabled on the real machine; the run is green on both invariants and nftables-drift.timer is listed for Mon 2026-08-31 00:00:00 CEST. Not yet observed across a real host reboot -- that was proven in vmbox.

verification.command: shellcheck -x --severity=style on every changed shell file
systemd-analyze verify on the rendered units
verification.evidence: No findings for either unit; the only output was pre-existing noise about unrelated host units.
gatelock-v0.7.3 is the newest tag; the pin now names it, which is what the freshness gate compares against.

risks: ExecStart hardcodes the repo path resolved at install time. Moving or renaming the checkout leaves the unit failing at every boot -- loudly, which is the correct direction, but it is a failure about the unit rather than about the firewall.

The host installation has not yet survived a real reboot; only the vmbox guest has. The first real reboot is the true test, and a false positive there would show as a failed unit rather than as a network outage.
allow-web/allow-dns now also (re)install the units, so those commands touch /etc/systemd/system where they previously did not.
rollback: sudo systemctl disable --now nftables-drift.timer && sudo systemctl disable nftables-drift.service
git revert the commit. After rollback: confirm `systemctl list-unit-files nftables-drift.*` reports nothing, and remember that `setup_wireguard_ssh.sh verify` is once again a check nobody runs.
